Federal Forage Fee Act of 1993 - Subjects grazing operations on Federal land to applicable Federal, State, and local environmental and land use requirements.

Fair Access to Investment Research Act of 2016 - Directs the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to revise its regulations to provide a "safe harbor" for investment fund research reports. The Act stipulates that a research report published by a broker or dealer regarding a covered investment fund shall not be deemed an offer for sale or an offer to sell a security, even if the broker or dealer is participating in the fund’s registered offering.

The legislation prohibits the SEC and self-regulatory organizations from imposing certain restrictive conditions on these reports, such as requirements related to the initiation of research coverage or specific registration periods. It further exempts such reports from certain filing requirements under the Investment Company Act of 1940, provided they adhere to established content standards. The Act includes provisions for interim effectiveness if the SEC fails to adopt the required revisions within 180 days. Finally, it specifies that these protections do not limit the applicability of federal antifraud or antimanipulation laws, nor do they restrict the oversight authority of self-regulatory organizations regarding broker or dealer conduct.
ref: Fair Access to Investment Research Act of 2016 This bill directs the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to revise a specified regulation to create a safe harbor for certain publications or distributions of research reports by brokers or dealers distributing securities. The revised regulation shall declare that a published or distributed investment fund research report shall not be deemed to constitute an offer for sale or an offer to sell a security that is the subject of the offering pursuant to an effective registration statement, even if the broker or dealer is participating or will participate in the registered offering of the covered investment fund's securities. The covered investment fund research report shall indeed be deemed to satisfy the regulation's requirements as well as those of any self-regulatory organization. The SEC shall not impose specified conditions and requirements when implementing the safe harbor.  Until the SEC has adopted such safe harbor revisions, and the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA) has revised a related rule, a covered investment fund shall be deemed to be a security listed on a national securities exchange that is not subject to a certain filing requirement of the Investment Company Act of 1940.

The credit is equal to 50 percent of the amount paid or incurred by an eligible for-profit organization to carry out qualified programs promoting economic and financial literacy for students. 

The Secretary of the Treasury, in consultation with the Secretary of Education, is authorized to award this credit to no more than 20 organizations per taxable year. A majority of recipients must be socially or economically disadvantaged small businesses, veteran-owned small businesses, women-owned small businesses, or entities with no more than $60 billion in assets. Priority is given to organizations serving urban or rural underserved areas. The bill stipulates that 25 percent of the credit amount must be used for direct activities, while 75 percent must be used for subgrants. It also includes provisions for coordination with other tax deductions or credits and mandates the issuance of necessary regulations. The amendments apply to taxable years beginning after the date of enactment.
ref: Promoting Financial Literacy and Economic Opportunity Act of 2015 This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow up to 20 for-profit organizations in any taxable year a business-related tax credit for 50% of the amount paid or incurred to carry out activities to improve the quality of student understanding of personal finance and economics. The Department of the Treasury shall determine which for-profit organizations are eligible for the credit, ensuring that a majority of credit recipients are: (1) either a socially and economically disadvantaged small business concern, a small business concern owned and controlled by women, or a small business concern that is at least 51% owned by veterans, or (2) do not have more than $60 billion in assets. In determining the eligibility of a for-profit organization, Treasury shall give priority to organizations that have programs serving either urban or rural underserved areas.

The bill authorizes states to share in qualified revenues from such production, requiring that at least 25 percent of these funds be used for specific conservation and infrastructure purposes. It further directs the Secretary to issue regulations for implementation, including procedures for gas-only leasing. The Act does not affect existing leases or marine sanctuaries.

Directs the Secretary of the Interior to issue implementing regulations, including procedures for entering into gas-only leases.

The bill adds criteria governing assessments of institutions under interim management, such as state-appointed receivers, ensuring that accreditation is not terminated solely based on the existence of such management. Additionally, the legislation requires that meetings, hearings, and appeals conducted by accrediting agencies and their subdivisions be open to public observation and comment, with agendas posted electronically at least seven days in advance. The Secretary of Education is authorized to issue regulations implementing these transparency requirements and ensuring due process protections are not reduced. Finally, the bill removes a deadline concerning the recognition of state accrediting agencies.
ref:
Amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to revise due process standards governing the accreditation process of educational institutions.

 Requires accrediting agencies and associations to provide educational institutions with: (1) written notice of deficiencies and a reasonable time period to correct such deficiencies; (2) advance notice of any adverse action and an opportunity for a hearing; and (3) a right to appeal an adverse action to an independent and impartial arbitration panel.

Requires accrediting agencies and associations to: (1) ensure consistent application of accreditation standards to an educational institution's governing board in receivership; and (2) allow public access to meetings involving accreditation recommendations.

pred: Contributions Legally Interdicted from Noncitizens To Our Nonprofits Act of 2016 (CLINTON Act of 2016) - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to revoke the tax-exempt status of "Federal official organizations" that knowingly or willingly accept or solicit contributions from persons connected to foreign governments. Defines a "Federal official organization" as any 501(c)(3) entity established, controlled, or actively managed by current or former high-level Federal officials, including the President, Vice-President, Members of Congress, Senate-confirmed appointees, certain White House staff, and Federal judges. Establishes a 20-year lookback period for officials and foreign government connections. Requires organizations that inadvertently accept such contributions to return them within 30 days of discovery to avoid losing tax-exempt status. Imposes a tax on organizations equal to the amount of any prohibited contribution knowingly or willingly accepted. Applies to contributions made after the date of enactment.
ref: Contributions Legally Interdicted from Noncitizens To Our Nonprofits Act of 2016 or the CLINTON Act of 2016  This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to prohibit a federal official organization from being treated as a tax-exempt organization under section 501(c)(3) for any period after the date on which the organization knowingly or willingly accepts or solicits any contribution from any person connected to a foreign government.  A tax-exempt organization is a "federal official organization" if one or more current or former specified federal officials established, control, or actively participate in the management of the organization.  If the organization accepts a contribution from any person and learns that that the person is connected to a foreign government after the acceptance, it will not be treated as knowingly or willingly accepting the contribution if the contribution is returned within 30 days of learning of the status of the person.  The bill imposes a tax on any federal official organization that knowingly or willingly accepts any contribution from any person connected to any foreign government in an amount equal to the amount of the contribution.

Prohibits Navy forces, beginning in FY2020, from including more than eight operational ballistic-missile submarines available for deployment. Prohibits the use of DOD funds for FY2014 or thereafter: (1) to maintain more than 250 submarine-launched ballistic missiles; (2) to maintain more than 150 intercontiental ballistic missiles (ICBMs) on a 24-hour, high alert status; or (3) for the medium extended air defense system. Amends the Internal Revenue Code with respect to political organizations to establish a campaign contribution limitation scheme applicable to the campaign committee of a candidate for election to the House of Representatives.  Provides that excess campaign contributions received by such an organization shall be included in its gross income. 
Amends the Communications Act of 1934 and Federal postal service law to condition the lowest unit charge for campaign ads upon a candidate's certification of compliance with such contribution limitation.
